meta.pos: noun; noun; verb; verb; verb; verb

defs.def: a person who has a university degree 大学毕业生；学士学位获得者

ex.s: 38   “I think a point that many people lose sight of is how easy it can be to fall behind schedule,” says graduate student Amanda Bindman.
ex.t: 38 “我认为很多人忽视的一点是，落后于计划是多么容易的事情，”研究生阿曼达·宾德曼说。

ex.s: In201, Melissa Ilardo, then a graduate student in genetics at the University of Copenhagen, heard about the Bajau.
ex.t: 201年，时任哥本哈根大学遗传学研究生的梅丽莎·伊拉尔多听说了巴哈乌人的情况。

ex.s: Jennifer is a first-generation graduate and an inspiration to her family—and that’s pretty powerful.
ex.t: 詹妮弗是家里的第一代大学毕业生，也是家人的鼓舞——这非常有力量。

ex.s: In China, a man from Jiangsu Province graduated from university at the age of 88, making him the oldest university graduate in the country.
ex.t: 在中国，一位来自江苏省的男子在88岁时大学毕业，成为全国最年长的大学毕业生。

ex.s: Trend of Chinese college graduates starting a business 1 What options do college students have after graduation?
ex.t: 中国大学毕业生创业趋势：大学毕业后学生有哪些选择？

ex.s: Farber, a graduate of Colorado State University, started out as a more conventional veterinarian.
ex.t: Farber是科罗拉多州立大学的毕业生，起初是一名较为传统的兽医。

ex.s: Lu returned to Shanghai in 1950 and, in 1965, graduated from Fudan University with a degree in English Language and Literature.
ex.t: 陆于1950年回到上海，1965年毕业于复旦大学，获英语语言文学学位。

ex.s: That willpower bore fruit when Jennifer graduated from University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire and became the first in her large family to earn a bachelor’s degree.
ex.t: 当詹妮弗从威斯康星大学欧克莱尔分校毕业、成为这个大家庭里第一个获得学士学位的人时，那份意志力结出了果实。

ex.s: Lisa graduated from our school last June and is about to go to college in New York.
ex.t: 丽莎去年6月从我们学校毕业，即将在纽约上大学。

ex.s: You are studying in a graduate program for a master's degree．
ex.t: 你正在攻读硕士学位的研究生项目中学习。

defs.def: a person who has completed their school studies 毕业生

ex.s: Maurice Ashley was kind and smart, a former graduate returning to teach, and this  48  was no game for him: he meant business.
ex.t: 莫里斯·阿什利善良而聪明，是回校执教的往届毕业生，对他来说这___48___绝非儿戏：他是认真的。

defs.def: to get a degree, especially your first degree, from a university or college 获得学位（尤指学士）；大学毕业

ex.s: If, at a later date, you wish to apply for a job or graduate school where an official copy of your UCLA record is required, it will be to your advantage to provide an impressive academic record.
ex.t: 如果在以后的日子里，你申请的工作或研究生院需要你的加州大学洛杉矶分校成绩单的正式副本，那么提供一份令人印象深刻的学业记录将对你有好处。

ex.s: Soon I will graduate and become part of the real world.
ex.t: 我很快就要毕业，成为现实世界的一部分。

defs.def: to complete a course in education, especially at high school 毕业（尤指中学）

ex.s: Through it all, she remained in good academic standing and graduated with honors.
ex.t: 在整个过程中她保持了良好的学术成绩并以优异成绩毕业。

ex.s: More than 750,000 have graduated from SAC, with many seeking employment in engineering, aviation, education, medicine and a wide variety of other professions.
ex.t: 超过750,000人从SAC毕业，许多人在工程、航空、教育等领域寻求就业……

ex.s: I know that Chinese is a very difficult language, but I hope to be fluent when I graduate.
ex.t: 我知道中文是一门很难的语言，但我希望毕业时能够说一口流利的中文。

ex.s: As soon as she graduated from high school she left home to live on Catalina Island off the Californian coast, away from her parents, where she enjoyed a life of sailing and off-road biking.
ex.t: 她一从高中毕业就离开家，住到加州海岸外的卡塔利娜岛上，远离父母，享受航海和越野骑行的人生。

defs.def: to give a degree, diploma, etc. to sb 授予（某人）学位（或毕业文凭等）
to start doing sth more difficult or important than what you were doing before 逐渐发展（或变化、进展、上升）

ex.s: When I applied to graduate school, I found three programmes promising to allow me to follow my desired research direction.
ex.t: 当我申请研究生院时，我发现有三个项目承诺允许我按照自己期望的研究方向发展。

ex.s: I quickly graduated from typical children’s books to ones with fewer pictures and longer chapters.
ex.t: 我很快就从典型的儿童读物过渡到图片较少、章节较长的书。

ex.s: Parry quickly graduated from his early hearts and sharks, and started to surprise families with drawings that captured young patients’ personalities.
ex.t: 帕里很快不再画最初的心形和鲨鱼，而是开始用捕捉小患者个性的画作给各个家庭带来惊喜。

chunks.cn: 国家的综合性）大学大学毕业生
